TODDLER 2 · LESSON 8

First Concepts for Toddlers: Big, Small, Up & Down

Age 18–24 MonthsSubject Think & TalkClass Toddler 2Duration 3–5 minutes

Around eighteen to twenty-four months, toddlers love spotting differences: the big ball and the little ball, the box that opens and shuts, the cup that is full and then empty. This class uses twelve realistic pictures arranged in six concept pairs — big and small, up and down, open and closed, full and empty, one and many, in and out — shown one at a time in exact pair order, so each opposite appears right after its partner and the comparison is easy to see.

There is no script and nothing to test. Show a pair, say the concepts clearly — ‘Big. Small.’ — and give your toddler time to look at the difference. Short, playful sessions of three to five minutes are all it takes.

PARENT INSTRUCTIONS

How to Teach First Concepts

Show the two cards in a pair one after the other and say the concept clearly. For example: ‘Big. Small.’ Give your toddler time to look at the difference.

Repeat the concepts naturally using real objects and everyday moments. You can show a big ball and a small ball, open and close a box, or point out when a cup is full or empty.

Keep the activity playful. Your toddler does not need to name every concept or answer questions correctly.

Every child develops differently. Kiddo School age ranges are guides, not tests or developmental deadlines.

TRY TOGETHER

Little things to say.

Prompts for you, not for the cards — say them softly while your baby looks.

  • Big ball. Small ball.
  • Up! Now down.
  • Open the box. Close the box.
  • The cup is full. Now it’s empty.
  • One duck. Many ducks.
  • The ball is in. Now the ball is out.
REAL-WORLD CONNECTION

Practice Around the House

Keep these activities parent-supervised and simple.

  • Big & Small: Find one big object and one small object.
  • Up & Down: Lift a toy up, then bring it down.
  • Open & Closed: Open and close a safe box or container together.
  • Full & Empty: Show a cup with water and an empty cup during an appropriate supervised activity.
  • One & Many: Show one toy, then a small group of toys.
  • In & Out: Put a toy in a basket, then take it out.
